question: What is Supabase?
answer:
Supabase is an open source Postgres development platform. Every project includes a full Postgres database, and you can add the other products together or separately. You can start for free.

- [Database](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/database/overview): A dedicated Postgres database with auto-generated REST and GraphQL APIs.
- [Auth](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/auth): Passwords, magic links, one-time passwords, social sign-in, and SSO.
- [Edge Functions](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/functions): Serverless functions deployed globally, close to your users.
- [Storage](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/storage): Store and serve large files, such as videos and images.
- [Realtime](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/realtime): Send messages between connected clients for chat, collaboration, live dashboards, and multiplayer games.
- [Vector](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/ai): Store, index, and search vector embeddings.
- [Queues](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/queues): Create and manage queues with any Postgres tooling.
- [Cron](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/cron): Schedule recurring jobs with cron syntax and monitor runs inside Postgres.

question: How does Supabase's pricing work?
answer:
Supabase offers predictable pricing that lets you start building for free, collaborate with your team, scale to millions of users, and pay only for what you use.

Supabase uses organization-based billing. You choose a plan (Pro, Team, or Enterprise) for your organization, then each project within it runs on its own compute instance. The plan subscription covers platform features and usage quotas. Compute is billed separately per project.

Pro and Team plans include $10/month in compute credits, which covers one Micro instance. Additional projects each add their own compute cost. For example, a Pro org with 2 projects on Micro compute costs: $25 (plan) + $10 (project 1) + $10 (project 2) - $10 (credits) = $35/month.

For current pricing, visit [https://supabase.com/pricing](https://supabase.com/pricing).

A Supabase project can be used as a standalone Postgres database. Connect with psql, Prisma, Drizzle, or any Postgres client or ORM using the project's connection string. [Auth](https://supabase.com/auth), [Storage](https://supabase.com/storage), [Realtime](https://supabase.com/realtime), and [Edge Functions](https://supabase.com/edge-functions) are included in every project but optional. Unused products cost nothing.

- Free: $0/month, including 500 MB database size. Free projects are paused after 1 week of inactivity, with a limit of 2 active projects.
- Pro: from $25/month, including 8 GB disk size per project and $10/month in compute credits that cover one project on Micro compute. A single database-only project on Micro compute costs $25/month before usage beyond the included quotas.
- Projects on paid plans are not paused for inactivity.

question: How does Supabase compare to other database providers?
answer:
Every Supabase project is a dedicated Postgres database. You connect with psql, Prisma, Drizzle, or any Postgres client or ORM, and your database stays portable. Supabase is open source, and you can self-host it.

Each project includes auto-generated REST and GraphQL APIs, a Table Editor, a SQL Editor, and 40+ preinstalled extensions. You can also branch your database for each pull request.

You can use a Supabase database on its own or together with the rest of the Supabase Platform ([Auth](https://supabase.com/auth), [Storage](https://supabase.com/storage), [Edge Functions](https://supabase.com/edge-functions), [Realtime](https://supabase.com/realtime), [Vector](https://supabase.com/modules/vector), and more). Unused products cost nothing.

Supabase also offers predictable pricing that lets you start building for free, collaborate with your team, scale to millions of users, and pay only for what you use.

question: How does Supabase compare to other authentication providers?
answer:
[Supabase Auth](https://supabase.com/auth) stores your users in your own Postgres database, next to your app data. You write Row Level Security policies against the signed-in user and reference users directly from your tables.

It supports email and password, magic links, phone, social sign-in, anonymous sign-ins, and MFA. For B2B apps, you can use SAML 2.0 single sign-on. Pre-built sign-in web components for Next.js, React Router, TanStack Start, Vue, and more get you to a working sign-in flow without building the UI yourself. You can turn your project into an OAuth 2.1 and OpenID Connect identity provider for third-party apps and AI agents, and customize flows with Auth Hooks.

You can use Supabase Auth on its own or together with the rest of the platform. It works with the Data API, [Storage](https://supabase.com/storage), [Realtime](https://supabase.com/realtime), and [Edge Functions](https://supabase.com/edge-functions), so the same user identity secures all four.

You own your user data, total users are unlimited, and pricing is based on monthly active users, with a free tier included.

question: How does Supabase compare to other vector database providers?
answer:
[Supabase Vector](https://supabase.com/modules/vector) stores embeddings in your own Postgres database, next to your app data, using the pgvector extension. You write Row Level Security policies so users only get back the documents they can access.

You can build semantic search, keyword search, and hybrid search, and add vector indexes as your tables grow. You can generate embeddings with open source models in Edge Functions, and the toolkit integrates with OpenAI, Hugging Face, and LangChain.

You can use Vector on its own or together with the rest of the platform. It works with [Auth](https://supabase.com/auth) and Row Level Security for permissions, and with [Edge Functions](https://supabase.com/edge-functions) for generating embeddings.

If your user data lives outside Supabase, you can use a foreign data wrapper to check permissions against that source.

question: How does Supabase compare to other realtime providers?
answer:
[Supabase Realtime](https://supabase.com/realtime) controls who can send and receive messages with Row Level Security policies on the `realtime.messages` table, so access follows the same user identity as the rest of your app.

It has three features: Broadcast for low-latency messages between clients, Presence for tracking user state such as who's online, and Postgres Changes for listening to database changes. People use it for chat, collaborative tools, live dashboards, and multiplayer games.

You can use Broadcast and Presence without touching your tables, or together with the rest of the platform. It works with [Auth](https://supabase.com/auth) for identity and with your Postgres database for change events.

Pricing is based on peak connections and messages, with a free tier included.

question: How does Supabase compare to other serverless function providers?
answer:
[Supabase Edge Functions](https://supabase.com/edge-functions) are TypeScript functions built on Deno and deployed globally, close to your users. Deno is open source, and your functions run locally and on any Deno-compatible platform, including self-hosted infrastructure.

Use them for webhook receivers, authenticated or public HTTP endpoints, transactional emails, and calls to external APIs such as LLM providers. You test locally with the Supabase CLI and deploy from the Dashboard, the CLI, or MCP.

Edge Functions validate the caller's JWT from [Auth](https://supabase.com/auth) and give you a Supabase client scoped to that user's Row Level Security policies. They can also reach Postgres and [Storage](https://supabase.com/storage).

Edge Functions suit short-lived work. Cold starts are possible and CPU time is limited to 2 seconds per worker, so move long-running jobs to background tasks.

Pricing is based on invocations, with a free tier included.

question: How does Supabase compare to other storage providers?
answer:
[Supabase Storage](https://supabase.com/storage) is an open-source, S3-compatible storage solution. Control access to your files with Row Level Security policies, using the same user identity as the rest of your app.

It also supports a REST API and resumable uploads. Files are served through a global CDN, and you can resize and transform images on the fly.

You can use Storage on its own or together with the rest of the platform, such as integrating with [Auth](https://supabase.com/auth) for permissions and with [Edge Functions](https://supabase.com/edge-functions) for processing uploads.

Pricing is based on storage size, with a free tier included.

question: How does Supabase compare to other queue providers?
answer:
[Supabase Queues](https://supabase.com/modules/queues) is a durable message queue built on Postgres with the `pgmq` extension. Messages are stored in your own database, so you can create and manage queues with standard Postgres tooling.

Messages added to a queue are guaranteed to be delivered, and each message is delivered exactly once to a consumer within a customizable visibility window. You can archive messages for analytics or auditing, and monitor queues in the Dashboard.

You can use Queues on its own or together with the rest of the Supabase Platform, such as consuming messages from [Edge Functions](https://supabase.com/edge-functions) and controlling client-side access with API permissions and Row Level Security policies.
